title: Coordinated deployment sprint synchronizer & signal protocol for runtime/console/api
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: Multiple teams (runtime, console, api) have independent sprint release windows which create collisions on shared infra (capacity, DB migrations, rollout traffic shaping). We need a lightweight synchronizer that maps sprint boundaries to a signal-driven release protocol so we can coordinate safe windows, reduce cross-team rollout flakiness, and tie launches back to OKRs and initiative timelines.

Goal: Define a compact operational spec (sprint synchronizer + signal protocol) that PMs and Eng leads can adopt to: 1) reserve bounded deployment slots, 2) standardize pre-launch signals (smoke, latency, error-rate, token-cost delta), 3) automate blackout windows and throttles in the release calendar, and 4) produce artifacts for OKR tracking and post-launch retros.

Scope: runtime, console, api teams for the April release train. Focus on: scheduling rules, signal definitions and thresholds, rollback / escalation criteria, calendar automation hooks (Calendar as Code), and ownership handoffs. Not in scope: provisioning systems or deep infra changes — we'll depend on ENG owners for implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A short spec published in Confluence with signal definitions and a schedule mapping that runtime/console/api leads approve
An automated calendar entry generator (Calendar-as-Code repo link) that creates reserved slots for the April train and marks blackout windows in team calendars
A rollout signal matrix (smoke, 95th latency, 5m error-rate, token-cost-delta) with numeric thresholds and automated monitoring dashboards linked
A tested escalation play that triggers canary rollback and notifies SRE/channel when thresholds breach during a canary within the reserved slot

decisions: Adopt a 3-tier slot model: small (10m), medium (45m), large (3h) for different change classes
Required signals during reserved slot: smoke (pass/fail) and 5m error-rate (hard thresholds). Latency and cost-delta are advisory for go/no-go unless the change touches runtime kernels.
Use Calendar-as-Code to create reserve blocks and a separate 'launch-control' calendar for the cross-team coordinator
Escalation path: Owner -> SRE on-call -> PM on-call -> Exec on-call with 15m SLA for notification
